# Email

Transactional email: a Mailer service on Cloudflare Email Service, printed to the console in development, plus invitation emails with organizations.

Id `extras/email`. It is one of the Extras: a project can have any number of them. Template: [`templates/extras/email/`](../../templates/extras/email/).

## What it is for

Send invitations, receipts and password resets. Call `send` on the `Mailer` service. In production the layer sends through Cloudflare Email Service; in development (`MAIL_TRANSPORT=console`) it prints each message to the dev server log. With organizations, invitations are emailed too.

## Add it

When you create the project:

```sh
npm create efforge my-app -- --extras=email
```

Add it to an existing project:

```sh
npx create-efforge add extras/email
```

## Needs

Nothing else.

## Conflicts with

Nothing.

## Service and layer

Your code asks for `Mailer`, declared in `packages/core/src/mailer.ts`. It has one member:

- `send(message)`. Fails with `MailerError`.

`MailerLive` implements it, and `efforge add` puts it in `AppLayer` in `apps/web/src/server/layers.ts`. Building the layer fails with `MailerConfigError` when a setting is missing or invalid.

- To test code that uses `Mailer`, give it a test layer: `Layer.succeed(Mailer, Mailer.of({ ... }))`. See [Swap a layer to test](../testing.md).
- To change the provider, write another layer for `Mailer` and use it in `layers.ts` in place of `MailerLive`.
- `MailerLive` already chooses between two implementations by `MAIL_TRANSPORT`. To add a provider, write another layer for `Mailer` in `apps/web/src/server/mailer.ts` and return it from `MailerLive` for a new `MAIL_TRANSPORT` value.

## Files it writes

`efforge add` writes these files.

| File | Only with |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/core/src/mailer.ts` | Always |
| `apps/web/src/server/mailer.ts` | Always |
| `apps/web/src/server/invitation-email.ts` | `auth=better-auth-orgs` |

## Files it edits

`efforge add` makes these edits with AST transforms (changes to the parsed code, not to its text), so it changes only what is listed and leaves the rest of each file alone.

### `packages/core/src/index.ts`

- Re-exports everything from `./mailer`.

### `apps/web/src/server/layers.ts`

- Adds `MailerLive` to `AppLayer`, imported from `./mailer`.

### `apps/web/src/server/auth.ts`

- Sets `sendInvitationEmail` in the options of the `organization` plugin. Only with `auth=better-auth-orgs`.

### `wrangler.jsonc`

- Adds a `send_email` entry: `{"name":"EMAIL"}`. Only with `infra=none`.

### `infra/alchemy.run.ts`

- Imports `* as Config` from `effect/Config`. Only with `infra=alchemy`.
- Declares `email` and binds it to the Worker as `EMAIL`. Only with `infra=alchemy`.
- Declares `mailFrom` and binds it to the Worker as `MAIL_FROM`. Only with `infra=alchemy`.
- Declares `mailTransport` and binds it to the Worker as `MAIL_TRANSPORT`. Only with `infra=alchemy`.

### `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`

- Passes the `MAIL_FROM` secret to the deploy job. Only with `infra=alchemy`.

### `AGENTS.md`

- Adds the rules under [Rules it adds to AGENTS.md](#rules-it-adds-to-agentsmd).

### `.env.example`

- Adds the environment variables listed below, each with its local value, or empty where it needs a real secret.

### `.dev.vars`

- Adds the same lines: `pnpm dev` reads them from here (gitignored). With Alchemy the file is `.env`.

### `efforge.jsonc`

- Records the add-on in the stack and the hashes of the files it wrote.

## Dependencies

None.

## Environment variables

- `MAIL_FROM`, for example `noreply@example.com`: Sender address; its domain must be enabled for Cloudflare Email Sending (wrangler email sending enable &lt;domain&gt;). Locally `noreply@localhost`.
- `MAIL_TRANSPORT`, for example `cloudflare`: cloudflare (default) sends through the EMAIL binding; console prints emails instead (the local value). Locally `console`.

## Package scripts

None.

## Rules it adds to AGENTS.md

### Email

- Send mail through the `Mailer` service from `@repo/core` (`send({ to, subject, text, html? })`); do not use the `EMAIL` binding directly. Always send a `text` body.
- `apps/web/src/server/mailer.ts` picks the transport from `MAIL_TRANSPORT`: `console` (set in `.dev.vars`) prints the message to the dev server log, anything else sends through Cloudflare Email Service with the `EMAIL` `send_email` binding. `MAIL_FROM` must be an address on a domain enabled for sending: `wrangler email sending enable <domain>`.
- Transactional mail only (invitations, receipts, password resets); use a dedicated platform for marketing or bulk sends.

Only with `auth=better-auth-orgs`:

#### Invitation emails

- `organization({ sendInvitationEmail })` in `auth.ts` calls `invitation-email.ts`, which emails the `/accept-invite/<id>` link through the `Mailer`. A failed send is logged and does not fail the invitation; the link is still shown to the inviter.

None known. The general ones are in [Status and limits](../limits.md).
